clue.text: Small-scale spring show where one may get a bite?

definitions.text: Small-scale spring show where one may get a bite?

parts.words: Small-scale spring show where one may get a bite?
parts.note: a miniature entertainment whose performers spring about, and where a spectator might be bitten by the cast

explanation.surface: A modest springtime exhibition where visitors might be nibbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, but it is the leaping of the tiny performers; 'Small-scale' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description of a sideshow of trained insects that jump and bite.

clue.text: Able to take the heat, following one reprimand?

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
I is the Roman numeral for one
a reproof is a scolding or reprimand

explanation.surface: Someone tolerating pressure after being told off once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can withstand heat without burning is resistant to flame.

clue.text: Get out more, having gained a little weight

parts.note: extra means additional, more
CT is the abbreviation for carat, a small unit of weight for gems

explanation.surface: Advice to go out more after putting on a few pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to draw or get it out.

clue.text: Pope in white

definitions.meaning: white symbolises purity, so someone in white is blameless

explanation.definitionFit: A papal name, and a word for guiltless, the quality white stands for.

clue.text: Direction if pursued likely to make an impact

definitions.text: Direction if pursued likely to make an impact

parts.words: Direction if pursued likely to make an impact
parts.note: a heading which, if kept to, ends in a crash rather than merely making an impression

explanation.surface: A path that, if followed, will make a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make an impact' suggests being influential; here it means a literal crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description of a heading that leads to a crash, also used figuratively for conflict.

clue.text: Start to sip convenient drink

indicators.note: the start of the word sip is its first letter

parts.note: handy means convenient, near at hand

explanation.surface: Begin by sipping a drink that is readily available.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink of beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub staple.

clue.text: Such frost the Ancient Mariner produced?

definitions.meaning: hoar frost formed when fog freezes on surfaces
the old spelling of a verse, as in the title of Coleridge's poem about the Mariner

explanation.surface: A question about what icy coating an old sailor made.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoar frost formed from freezing fog, and the old spelling of a verse in Coleridge's title.

clue.text: A social event of signal quality

definitions.meaning: a formal party, such as one after a wedding
how well a radio or phone picks up a broadcast

explanation.definitionFit: Both a formal gathering and the clarity with which broadcasts are picked up.

clue.text: Master arrested seaman — top removed for application of lashes

indicators.note: something arrested is held, so the master grips the next piece inside it

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts, a degree

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of the word is its first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a lascar is an East Indian sailor

explanation.surface: A ship's master detains a sailor and takes his cap before a flogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrested' looks like a police arrest but means holding inside; 'lashes' suggests flogging a seaman, yet it is eyelashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up applied to the eyelashes, rather than a whipping.

clue.text: Not absurd to be left on desert island

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one piece on another places it after

parts.note: to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship
Iona is a Hebridean island

explanation.surface: Being marooned on a desert island is no absurd idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like an adjective for the island but is a verb here; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sensible and logical is the opposite of absurd.

clue.text: A line's told to charge

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a cue is an actor's line, so this gives a cue's

explanation.surface: Someone is informed of a line on which to make a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To accuse someone is to charge them with an offence.

clue.text: Plant taking time to decompose into this?

definitions.text: Plant taking time to decompose into this?

parts.note: the pea is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: Vegetation slowly breaking down over many years.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: plants decompose over time into this soil material.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly decayed plant matter accumulating in bogs is the material described.

clue.text: Youngster spread out simple task

parts.note: a child is a youngster
to splay is to spread out

explanation.surface: A youngster sprawls out with an easy job.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something very easy to do.

clue.text: Where peacock has eyes, captivating female with no delay

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: the eye-spots of a peacock are on its tail
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A peacock's eyes charm a peahen at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivating' puts HEN inside TAIL, after ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for paying promptly, immediately, without waiting.

clue.text: Small beer problem leads to ropy bit of work

parts.note: a half is a half-pint of beer in a British pub
a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: A minor drinking issue causes a poor piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ropy' looks like British slang for shoddy, but it means made of rope; 'leads to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple knot tied in a rope, so literally a piece of ropework.

clue.text: I gave Solomon materials for Temple — employ 'em soundly

definitions.text: I gave Solomon materials for Temple

indicators.note: said soundly signals the words are taken by how they are pronounced

parts.note: to employ is to hire, so this gives hire 'em

explanation.surface: A king boasts of supplying Solomon's building, urging others to take on workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical king of Tyre supplied cedar and craftsmen for Solomon's Temple.

clue.text: Liqueur gets one Brontë sister into trouble

indicators.note: into places the sister inside the word for trouble

parts.note: mire is a mess or difficulty
a means one
the Brontës published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell

explanation.surface: A drink lands one of the literary sisters in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Each Brontë sister used the pen-surname Bell, so one of them is A BELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum brandy distilled from small yellow plums of the same name.

clue.text: Under aperture, fit radio

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece under another is placed after it

parts.note: a port is an opening, as a porthole
able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: Instructions to mount a radio beneath an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable is a small carry-around radio or television.

clue.text: I shall follow Friar Tuck

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so this piece goes second

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Friar
I'll is the contraction of I shall

explanation.surface: A Robin Hood fan vows to follow the jolly Friar Tuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friar Tuck' looks like one name, but Tuck is the definition, a fold sewn in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck and a frill are both decorative gathered folds in dressmaking.

clue.text: Musical group's grave expression, joining one opera company

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is carved on gravestones
I is the Roman numeral for one
ENO is English National Opera

explanation.surface: A band's solemn words on joining an opera company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like solemn, but it is the burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: In Baroque music the full orchestra, as opposed to the soloists of the concertino.

clue.text: Tune once played at hunter's last meet

indicators.note: a tune played may be rearranged, so the letters are reworked
the last of hunter's is its final letter

explanation.surface: A hunting tune is played at the end of the hunt meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges TUNEONCE into ENCOUNTE, and the R from 'hunter's last' ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone, often unexpectedly, is to come across them.

clue.text: Warm garment for turret?

parts.note: a sleeveless knitted pullover, whose name read literally describes the upper part of an armoured vehicle

explanation.surface: A question about clothing to keep a gun turret warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless jumper, and literally the turret on top of an armoured tank.

clue.text: A series of clues affording progress

parts.note: a scent is a trail of clues followed by a tracker

explanation.surface: A run of crossword clues allows advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing upward is progress, an advance.

clue.text: Expecting whale to blow here?

definitions.meaning: a whale blows its spray from its blowhole, or spout

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for pregnant, and literally at a whale's blowhole.

clue.text: Act of rudeness, rejecting food at teatime

indicators.note: rejecting sends the food back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: buns are sweet rolls eaten at afternoon tea

explanation.surface: Refusing to eat at teatime is impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate slight or rebuff is an act of rudeness.

clue.text: Scowling, crush insect

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: frowning with jutting brows, a heavy mallet for crushing, and a hard-shelled insect.

clue.text: Answer objection in subsequent comeback

indicators.note: in places the objection inside the reversed piece
a comeback turns back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: later means subsequent
but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Responding to a complaint in a later retort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Answer' at the front looks like a verb, but it is the noun definition; 'comeback' also fits the surface as a retort.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is an answer refuting an argument.

clue.text: Not keen as auctioneer's eighth item may appear

parts.note: a lot is an item sold at auction
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Reluctance shown by an auctioneer over item eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as auctioneer's ... may appear' is a link explaining why an item is a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctant or unwilling, an old variant spelling of loath.

clue.text: Play pass behind to indicated place

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so this piece goes second

parts.note: there is a place pointed out
to lapse is to pass, as time passes

explanation.surface: Sport instruction: play a pass back to a marked spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb but is the definition: a Restoration comedy by Vanbrugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1696 comedy by John Vanbrugh.
